original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: For five sources and all 31 nonzero paired-readout masks, does adding the arity-four source call Q_r: z += sum_{j != r} B_j x_j lower the complete ledger when each Q_r pays one dispatch and four source-map additions?
scope_change_reason: Refines the broad card to the five-source complement arity-four call, disjoint from the retained pair/trio/frame results and complementary to open PR #2249, whose high-arity floor is for six sources.
bottleneck_link: docs/research/research-family-status.md: New coding, geometry and recursive boundaries / retain exploration; the result tests whether a paid connector alphabet change removes any cost in the all-mask caller.
stop_rule: Stop this family at the five-source uniform charged ledger unless an actual caller supplies nonuniform source tariffs or a cheaper legal fused implementation. Do not infer a supplier or global obstruction from this local result.
evidence: The original 945-pairing verifier passes. A dirty two-dimensional four-source call control passes. The exact normalized one-Q/eight-singleton branch contains 23,184 words with maximum prefix-difference set size 26/32. Pair-count and parity bounds cover all remaining event-count cases and prove every schedule using Q costs at least 149 ledger units, versus the predecessor's exact 148-unit baseline.

open_questions.question: For an actual five-source caller with nonuniform B-map prices, can the complement arity-four family beat the complete caller bill?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The present bound uses one uniform unit per source-map addition and dispatch. A real caller might price source subsets differently, which could change whether this operation saves anything.
open_questions.first_step: Bind a concrete caller's five complete B-map prices, dispatch cost and program-storage cost, then enumerate only event profiles that survive those prices.
open_questions.blocked_by: No eligible five-source caller or legal implementation boundary for Q_r is identified in this checkout; further enumeration has no supplier decision to change until that contract exists.
